prompts.text: What's the cutest harmless reason you've found to message someone you liked?
Tell me about an opening message that made you smile before you even replied.
A playful voice note or a clever one-line message from someone you're getting to know?
We both keep typing and deleting our first message. Who would you bet presses send first?
People sometimes spend longer choosing an emoji than writing the actual message.
A simple thoughtful message is better than an elaborate line someone copied from elsewhere.
What sort of good-morning message would feel natural rather than rehearsed?
Recall receiving a message with a small detail the sender remembered about you.
You get a reply full of emojis and no explanation. How would you playfully ask what it means?
An unexpected photo of something that reminded them of you or a short check-in after a busy day?
What small detail about someone makes you think you'd enjoy spending more time together?
Describe realising you liked somebody because of the way they treated another person.
Someone who makes you laugh during a dull errand or someone who remembers your favourite snack?
We have ten minutes to get to know each other at a crowded event. What question would you save for last?
People sometimes become attractive through ordinary gestures rather than dramatic entrances.
Remembering a person's boundaries says more than remembering their favourite colour.
Which everyday habit of yours would someone find endearing after getting to know you?
Recall a moment someone noticed something thoughtful you'd done without mentioning it.
We're both trying to appear relaxed during a first meeting. Who do you think gives it away first?
An easy conversation filled with laughter or a surprisingly thoughtful question?
What's a date idea that would feel fun even if both people were nervous?
Tell me about a simple outing that became memorable because of the company.
Browse a weekend market together or try a board-game café for the first time?
We plan to meet outdoors and it starts raining. What's our backup plan?
A short activity together often makes first-date conversation less formal.
A first date shouldn't require either person to spend beyond their comfort.
What activity would let somebody learn your playful side without too much pressure?
Describe the funniest harmless misunderstanding you've had while arranging a meeting.
We realise we've accidentally booked seats for completely different films. How would you rescue the evening?
An afternoon coffee with no strict ending or a planned two-hour outing?
What kind of compliment would make you smile without knowing how to respond?
Tell me about a compliment you replayed in your head long after the conversation ended.
Have somebody admire your sense of humour or notice the effort behind something you've made?
We must compliment each other without mentioning appearance. What would you start with?
A specific compliment often feels more personal than a dramatic declaration.
A genuine compliment doesn't need a perfect moment.
What's something about your personality you wish people noticed sooner?
Recall somebody appreciating a quality you rarely think about yourself.
You get to leave one short note for somebody you're beginning to like. What would it say?
A handwritten compliment on a small card or a thoughtful message after your first outing?
What's the funniest way somebody has tried to hide a crush?
Describe a time a friend recognised your interest in somebody before you admitted it.
Have friends tease you gently about a crush or keep the whole thing private?
Your friends unexpectedly invite the person you like to a group outing. How would you keep your composure?
People sometimes become unusually formal around someone they normally speak to easily.
Trying to look completely unbothered often makes a crush more obvious.
Which tiny mistake would instantly reveal that you're nervous around somebody?
Recall giving yourself a pep talk before a conversation that turned out easy.
You accidentally call someone you like by a nickname you only use in your head. How do you recover?
Make eye contact and smile first or start talking and hope the nerves fade?
What's a question you'd like someone to ask before planning a surprise for you?
Describe a moment somebody respected your preferences and made the plan better.
A thoughtful surprise within an agreed plan or a completely spontaneous outing?
I want to suggest a second date without knowing your schedule. What's the least awkward way to ask?
A comfortable invitation leaves room for the other person to decline without embarrassment.
A low-pressure invitation is often more attractive than an impressive proposal.
What makes it easy for you to say yes to spending time with someone?
Tell me about an invitation that felt considerate because the person knew your routine.
We both suggest places to meet and choose the same one. What would you read into the coincidence?
Pick the next date together or take turns choosing the activity?
Which harmless competitive activity would bring out your playful side?
Tell me about losing a game and still having more fun than the winner.
Play a two-person trivia game or challenge each other to a silly drawing contest?
We compete to find the best inexpensive dessert. How should we judge our choices?
People sometimes show their funniest reactions when they're terrible at a game.
Being a good sport matters more than winning a friendly date challenge.
What game would you want a potential partner to play with you once?
Recall someone making a boring activity enjoyable through a spontaneous competition.
Our first shared quiz ends in a tie. What should the tie-breaker be?
A playful dance lesson or a beginner cooking challenge together?
What's a small sign a conversation is turning into a connection for you?
Describe a chat that started lightly but left you curious about the other person.
Exchange funny childhood stories or talk about an unusual shared interest?
We each ask three questions and must invent a fourth based on the answers. What's your first one?
Interest often shows through follow-up questions rather than dramatic statements.
You don't have to reveal everything about yourself during the first few conversations.
Which topic makes you forget to check how much time has passed?
Recall a conversation where an unexpected point of agreement made you feel closer.
We realise it's late but neither person wants to end the call. How would you suggest finishing it?
An unhurried phone call or a long exchange of messages throughout the evening?
What kind of playful teasing makes you feel closer to somebody?
Tell me about an inside joke that began during an early conversation.
Let somebody give you a funny nickname or invent one together?
We realise we have opposite views about a harmless everyday choice. How would you turn it into a running joke?
Teasing works best when both people understand what topics are off limits.
Someone respecting a boundary is more charming than somebody testing it.
What joke would you only make once you knew somebody well enough to appreciate it?
Describe a time someone laughed at themselves and made the whole conversation easier.
You accidentally tease me about something I find sensitive. How would you want to put it right?
A shared silly catchphrase or a recurring question at the start of every call?
What's something you'd enjoy looking forward to with somebody you're getting to know?
Recall the first moment you realised another person was becoming part of your routine.
Plan a casual weekend outing or agree to watch the same film and discuss it afterwards?
We both keep finding reasons to continue our conversation. What friendly challenge would you suggest next?
Early connections often develop through small repeat encounters rather than grand milestones.
It's fine to enjoy getting to know someone without rushing to label everything.
What helps you decide whether you want to see somebody again?
Describe a goodbye that made you look forward to your next meeting.
Our first outing ends with an unfinished story. What's a playful way to follow up later?
A message saying you enjoyed the day or an invitation to continue the conversation next week?
